<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json baae6ed14e90e357b6e437e62aed01f0f1be9649` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `92ffe4401dbdd7c59da1a8b16e69cd727632cadb` — the merge of head `d613a6d86bb2c1bf9b03da51ef531e0d7d1bd9e8` into base `baae6ed14e90e357b6e437e62aed01f0f1be9649`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 92ffe4401dbdd7c59da1a8b16e69cd727632cadb && git checkout 92ffe4401dbdd7c59da1a8b16e69cd727632cadb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin baae6ed14e90e357b6e437e62aed01f0f1be9649 d613a6d86bb2c1bf9b03da51ef531e0d7d1bd9e8 && git checkout -B drift-repro baae6ed14e90e357b6e437e62aed01f0f1be9649 && git merge --no-ff d613a6d86bb2c1bf9b03da51ef531e0d7d1bd9e8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json baae6ed14e90e357b6e437e62aed01f0f1be9649
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs baae6ed14e90e357b6e437e62aed01f0f1be9649` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d613a6d86bb2c1bf9b03da51ef531e0d7d1bd9e8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-organization.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/feature-gate-guard.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-organization-rename-action.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/platform-objects.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/organization-rename-single.dogfood.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (read unchanged, for the served flags), packages/qa/dogfood/test/org-record-admin-reach.dogfood.test.ts (read unchanged, the multi-boot claimant)

Face: schema — `reviewFace` on the 12-path file list hits the one spec path. The rest of the diff (the two changesets, the four generated bundles, `sys-organization-name-timezone-help.test.ts`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Inputs: card #25347 (body and all 7 comments; ruling 6384629949, claim 6384658457, seat pointer 6384842854, os-dev-report 6384984186), PR #25661 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at the head; merge-base `49653f91`, base `baae6ed1`), and the 40 check-runs on the head (read twice; the second read is the state recorded in ③).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The spec row move — right, and exactly the ruling's widening.** `public-auth-features.ts` changes by +5/−3: the row `'sys_organization.actions.rename_organization'` leaves `multiOrgEnabled.gatedInputs` and enters `organization.gatedInputs`, with its comment. Nothing else moves: `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURE_NAMES` (the `requiresFeature` enum), both entries' `semantics: 'default-on'`, `FEATURE_GATE_OPERATORS` and `featureGatePredicate` are untouched. `multiOrgEnabled.gatedInputs` still books exactly `create_organization`, `update_organization`, `delete_organization`, `set_active_organization` and `leave_organization`; the object declares those five on `requiresFeature: 'multiOrgEnabled'` (head lines 80, 102, 122, 143, 216), and `change_slug` stays the cloud composition's.

2. **The gate it mirrors — right.** `sys-organization.object.ts` moves only `rename_organization.requiresFeature` to `'organization'`. `requiresMembershipReach: 'update_organization'` (owner, admin), the target `/api/v1/auth/organization/update`, `bodyShape` and the params (`name`, `logo`, no `slug`) are unchanged. The lowered predicate goes from `(ADMINS) && features.multiOrgEnabled != false` to `(ADMINS) && features.organization != false`.

3. **What the move widens, measured against the served flags.** plugin-auth's `getPublicConfig()` serves `organization = pluginConfig.organization ?? true` and `multiOrgEnabled = postureEnforcesWall(tenancyPosture)`. So under `single` with the organization plugin on, the door is now offered where it was hidden — the one widening ruling 6384629949 allows. Under `group` and `isolated` both flags are true before and after, so nothing changes. With the organization plugin off, the door is now hidden where the old gate would have shown it under a wall posture — a configuration in which the `organization/*` endpoints do not exist, so this is the same capability gate every other `organization` input already carries, not a boundary change. No other input's gate moves.

4. **No access boundary is loosened.** The feature gate is a console affordance (a lowered `visible` predicate); the server door is better-auth's `organization/update`, which was never posture-gated. The PR's ablation records the door admitting the rename on both trees, and the dogfood pin records a plain member refused 403 `YOU_ARE_NOT_ALLOWED_TO_UPDATE_THIS_ORGANIZATION`. Grades are unchanged. `rename_organization` was not booked under `cloudManaged` before and is not now; the slug door is untouched.

5. **The guard that binds the row and the gate — satisfied in both directions.** `feature-gate-guard.test.ts` forward: the `organization` row resolves to the action and its predicate carries `features.organization != false` as a top-level conjunct. Reverse: the action's only `features.*` reference is `organization`, booked there; no stale `multiOrgEnabled` booking remains. The floor of 37 referenced inputs is unchanged by a move. It runs in the Test Core shards (in progress at read time, see ③).

6. **Pins — moved with the gate, no weakening.** The action pin now asserts `(reach) && features.organization != false` with `update_organization` on `multiOrgEnabled` as the control; the matrix row is `${ADMINS} && ${ORG}`; the multiOrg roster test keeps its gated side (every action whose predicate names `features.multiOrgEnabled`) and filters its pinned side to the `MULTI_ORG` rows, so the five multi-org actions are still pinned as the whole multi-org surface. Other claimants read at the head and unaffected: `org-record-admin-reach.dogfood.test.ts` (multi boot, `organization: true` there, so the rename still shows for owner and admin and the grade still hides it from a member), `org-change-slug-bound-action` (header order unchanged), `organization-rename-door`, `confirm-question-carryover.test.ts`. No ADR anchor names either file; no checked-in spec artifact lists the rows (the only match outside `src/` is a TS2339 debt entry in `test-typecheck-debt.json`); no hand-written doc ties the rename to multi-org.

7. **Public TS surface.** `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES` is a published const: the literal type of `organization.gatedInputs` gains a member and `multiOrgEnabled.gatedInputs` loses one. No export is added, removed or renamed, and nothing an author or a consumer sends is newly refused, so this is not an accept-set narrowing; `check:api-surface` is the mechanical check, and its job, `Type Check · consumer gates`, completed green on this head.

### ② Semver level

Two changesets, `@objectstack/spec` patch and `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch, each carrying `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; the PR body carries the same two lines. **Right.** `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: the `requiresFeature` enum is unchanged, and no key, value or type an author writes is added, refused or re-meant; the registry rows are not authorable. The level follows the kind alone (ruling A on #25105; AGENTS.md Post-Task 3): `none` takes `patch`, and the widening is non-protocol, so it ships `patch`. `Clause-②: yes` with no arm is a well-formed widening in `clause2-line.mjs` (the arm is optional; the file's older arm docblock still says a widening takes `minor`, superseded by its own header and AGENTS.md — not this PR's text). No `(narrowing)` arm, no BREAKING banner, no ADR-0087 disposition owed; `Check Changeset` is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **os-dev-report 6384984186:** `open_questions: []`, `out_of_scope_findings: []` — no dev flag to answer. The one open question of the earlier report 6368023747 (the cross-lane spec row) is what ruling 6384629949 decided and this diff lands.
- **Ruling conditions 1–6:** (1) the PR body's "Outside the claim's file surface" section cites 6384629949 — met. (2) the declaration on spec seat post #6017 — the report's `api_writes` records it; #6017 is outside this brief's inputs, so it is not verified here: the owning seat confirms it before queueing. (3) this record. (4) `mode:cloud` — declared in claim 6384658457. (5) the action pin, the matrix row and the multiOrg roster test move with the gate — verified in the diff. (6) `organization-rename-single.dogfood.test.ts` on a plain showcase boot — read; its four cases cover the served flags, the console-side predicate for admin and member, the member's 403 and the admin's 200 with the slug kept. It ran locally only: the CI dogfood shards skip on `pull_request` and `merge_group` by design (ci.yml:2128), so its first CI run is post-merge.
- **Check-runs on the head (second read, 2026-10-24T13:58Z):** 40 runs — 26 success, 7 skipped, 7 in progress: Test Core 1–6 (where `feature-gate-guard.test.ts` and the spec and platform-objects suites run) and Type Check · workspace. Completed green since the first read: Build Core, Type Check · source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · docs & code guards, and the two scoped lints. None completed red. This record judges the diff; the queue guard still requires every check green, so the seven in-progress runs gate the landing mechanically and this record does not stand in for them.
- **Author:** `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; head repo is the base repo (not a fork); the PR is a draft with auto-merge off.
- **Overlap:** #25626 and #25637 touch neighbouring lines and assert nothing about this action; `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path` is green.
- Noted, not blocking: the new `name` help names a door only owners and admins are offered, so a plain member reads a pointer to a button they do not see. UX copy, not a contract matter.
